title: Manifest
description: The complete pipeline manifest parsed from manifest.toml.

defaults.description: Default values applied to all steps unless overridden.

message.description: Error message shown when constraint is violated

category.description:
Free-form label for grouping failures across runs, e.g. `quality`, `network`.

Deliberately unconstrained and never interpreted: nothing in the engine branches on
it, so a fixed vocabulary would only reject labels a vendor's dashboard finds useful.

code.description:
Unique error code. `A-Z`, `0-9` and `_` only: the stdlib resolves a code by looking
this name up verbatim in `FLOWRS_ERROR_MAP`, so any other character would be
unreachable from `die`. Enforced in `validate::errors`.

exit_code.description:
Process exit code that signals this error (author band: 1..=63, unique).
A step exits with this code to report the error; the engine maps it back.

max_retries.description: Max retries for this error type (overrides step-level retries)

retryable.description: Should the step be retried on this error?

oneOf.description: Error condition, step fails but pipeline may continue

GroupDef.description: Parameter group definition for UI organization.

description.description: Prose explaining what the group contains.

ParamDef.description: A parameter definition from the manifest.

readonly.description:
If true, user cannot override via -p or -c.
Value is resolved normally (base default → profile override).

PipelineHooks.description:
Lifecycle hooks for pipeline execution.

**Four hooks, because an author asks four questions.** Each is a side-channel reaction: never
subject to `-s`/`-e`/`-k`, never in `status.json`'s step map, and its failure warns and never
fails the run — no exceptions. Work whose success is part of what the run delivers is a *step*
(a DAG step, or `teardown = true`), where failure semantics and targeting are available. System
cleanup on cancellation is the engine's, guaranteed by the signal handler and the Drop chain, and
is neither.

`deny_unknown_fields` so a removed or misspelled hook name is a parse error. A silently ignored
`on_finish` would drop the author's close-out work without saying so.

on_error.description:
A step failed with a specific resolved error: `error_code -> [scripts]`.

Purely a failure response — a cancelled step bypasses it, because the operator stopping the
run is not a fault.

on_failure.description:
The run did not succeed, however it ended badly — step failure, teardown delivery failure,
or the operator's cancellation.

A cancelled run's `128 + N` reaches the script as `EXIT_CODE`, alongside `FAILED_STEP` and
`status.json`'s `cancelled_by`, so one script branches on the outcome.

on_start.description:
Announce that the run exists: fired once the pipeline is unpacked, before parameter
resolution and the profile detector.

Earliest point at which the hook scripts are readable — for a package they are inside the
encrypted payload — so it is also the earliest a hook can fire at all. A "run started"
notification sent from a DAG step would be silent for a run that died in resolution.

Sees the engine-provided paths but **not** resolved params: resolution has not run yet.

cache_dir.description:
Directory name, relative to `WORK_DIR`, holding results shared across runs.

Required for any step that sets `cache = true`. Declared once at the pipeline level
rather than per step so every cached step lands in one place a user can inspect or
delete, and so the name is a property of the pipeline rather than a detail repeated
at each use.

min_threads.description: Minimum number of threads required to run this pipeline.

profile.description: Pipeline-defined profile for profile-specific parameter defaults.

requires.description:
External tools and libraries the pipeline's steps invoke.

Advisory metadata: declaring a requirement does not install it, and nothing is
checked during a run. `flowrs inspect --check-environment` reports what is missing,
on the machine that will actually execute the steps. Activating whatever provides
them — a module system, a conda environment, a container — stays the operator's job;
FlowRs only inherits `PATH`.

Profile.description:
A pipeline-defined profile that drives profile-specific parameter defaults.

The profile references a param (which should have `enum` values defined),
provides a detector script for auto-detection, and maps values to profiles.

detector.description: Detector script path relative to `bin/` directory.

param.description: Name of the parameter that acts as profile (must exist in `[params]`).

profiles.description:
Maps profile names to their member values.
e.g., `{ "ngs": ["SINGLE", "PAIRED"], "tgs": ["TGSONT", "TGSPACBIO"] }`

timeout.description:
Maximum seconds to wait for the detector script before failing.
Defaults to `DEFAULT_DETECTOR_TIMEOUT_SECS`. Set higher for detectors that
scan large datasets or access slow/remote filesystems.

unassigned_ok.description:
Permit enum values of the profile param that belong to no profile.

By default every enum value must be assigned to exactly one profile: a value in none is
detectable but selects no profile, so the run silently uses base defaults for every
profile-specific param — the author's `[params.X.ngs]` blocks simply do not apply, with
nothing saying so.

Set this when that is intended, e.g. a value handled entirely by base defaults. It
relaxes the manifest check only; detection of an unassigned value still **warns** at run
time, naming the value and the fallback. The escape hatch is for authors who accept the
behaviour, not a way to silence the report of it.

Requirements.description:
External tools and libraries a pipeline needs, grouped by how presence is established.

Three groups rather than one list with a `type` field: each is probed by a different
mechanism (a `PATH` lookup, an interpreter import, a loader query), and the TOML reads as
the sections a pipeline author already thinks in.

Versions are deliberately absent. A constraint is only worth writing down if it can be
checked, and there is no portable way to ask an arbitrary bioinformatics tool its version
— `samtools --version`, `bwa` with no argument, and `fastqc --version` disagree on both
the flag and the format. Recording constraints that are never enforced would be worse
than recording none: it reads as a guarantee. Presence is what FlowRs can honestly check,
so presence is what the schema expresses.

python.description:
Python modules that must import, e.g. `["numpy", "pysam"]`.

Import names, not distribution names: `Bio`, not `biopython`.

r.description: R packages that must load, e.g. `["ggplot2", "dplyr"]`.

tools.description: Executables that must resolve on `PATH`, e.g. `["samtools", "bwa"]`.

StepDef.description: A single step in the pipeline workflow.

cache.description:
Reuse this step's results across runs when its inputs are unchanged.

A cached step writes to `${CACHE_DIR}`, a directory keyed by everything that can
change its output (see `cache_key`). When a run finds a completed entry for that key
it skips the step and downstream steps read the existing results.

cache_key.description:
Parameters whose values are part of this step's cache identity.

Only these participate — deliberately not every resolved param. Hashing all of them
would invalidate a QC step because an unrelated downstream threshold changed, which
defeats the point of caching. Declaring the list is the author's statement of what
this step actually reads.

The step's executable content and the identity of its cached upstreams are always
included, so editing a script or invalidating an upstream invalidates this step
without anything being declared here.

depends_on.description: Step names that must complete before this step

exec.description: Executable filename relative to pipeline's steps/ directory

outputs.description:
Expected output files this step should produce (optional).
Paths must use allowed variables: ${OUT_DIR}, ${WORK_DIR}, ${TMP_DIR},
and ${CACHE_DIR} for a cached step.
If declared, FlowRs will check these files exist after step completion.
Missing required outputs convert a successful exit (0) into a failure.

retries.description: Number of retry attempts on failure (0 = no retries).

retry_delay.description: Delay in seconds between retry attempts.

teardown.description: If true, this step runs after the main pipeline completes (success or failure).

threads.description: Thread allocation: "auto" (use CLI value) or fixed number.

threads_weight.description:
Relative share of the budget among `"auto"` steps ready in the same scheduling pass.

A ratio, not a thread count: weights are meaningful only against the other members of the
cohort, so they scale with `-@` rather than pinning a number. Two ready steps weighted 3 and
1 split what is available 3:1 — six and two threads under `-@ 8`, three and one under `-@ 4`.

Absent means 1, which is the equal split that has always been the behaviour. A weight
therefore only has an effect when two or more `"auto"` steps are ready together and at least
one of them declares something other than 1.

Contradictory with a fixed `threads`, and rejected as such: a fixed cost already states the
exact number of permits the step wants, leaving no share to divide.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds. Step is killed if it exceeds this duration.

trigger_rule.description: Trigger rule determining when this step should execute

StepDefaults.description: Default values applied to all steps unless overridden at the step level.

retries.description: Default number of retry attempts for all steps.

retry_delay.description: Default delay in seconds between retry attempts.

timeout.description: Default timeout in seconds for all steps.

ThreadAllocation.description: Thread allocation: the string "auto" to use the CLI-provided thread count, or a fixed thread count of at least 1.

TriggerRule.description: Trigger rule determining when a step should execute.

oneOf.description: All upstream tasks must complete (any state)
At least one upstream task must succeed
At least one upstream task must fail
No upstream tasks failed (success or skipped OK)
No failures and at least one success
Always execute regardless of upstream states
